provisions.title: Short Title, Extent and Commencement

Legal Provision: This Act is called the Factories Act, 1948.
It extends to the whole of India.
It came into force on 1st April 1949.
Objective: To provide a uniform legal framework regulating working conditions in factories across India.
Explanation: It ensures that all factories across India are governed by the same statutory framework.
HR / Industrial Relations Significance: Ensures uniform compliance for HR departments nationwide.
Forms the legal base for all factory-related HR policies.

provisions.title: Definitions

Legal Provision: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.
Important Definitions: Any person employed directly or indirectly in manufacturing or related work
Person with ultimate control over factory affairs
Making, altering, repairing, finishing, packing, washing, or otherwise treating an article
Objective: To clearly define legal terms so that applicability of the Act is precise.
Explanation: This is the most important section of the Act, as every compliance depends on these definitions.
If a person is not a “worker”, he is not protected under the Act.
If an establishment is not a “factory”, the Act does not apply.
HR Significance: Impacts payroll, compliance, safety, and inspections
